title: Raspberry and Lime Iced Tea
changes_from_base: Black tea sweetened with a strained raspberry syrup and sharpened with lime juice, in place of lemon and mint.
summary: Black iced tea turned pink and fruity with a seedless raspberry syrup and a good squeeze of lime.

steps.title: Tea
steps.text: Steep the tea bags in the boiling water for 4 minutes, take them out, add the cold water and set aside to cool.

steps.title: Raspberry syrup
steps.text: Bring the raspberries, sugar and water to a simmer, crushing the berries with a spoon, and let it bubble for 3 minutes until saucy. A short cook releases the juice and colour without a jammy taste.

steps.title: Strain
steps.text: Press the mixture through a fine sieve to catch the seeds, then stir in the lime juice and leave to cool.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Stir the syrup into the cooled tea, taste for sweetness and add a little more sugar if needed, then chill.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pour over ice and add slices of lime.

tips: Skipping the sieve leaves seeds floating in every glass, so take the extra minute.
Frozen raspberries are ideal here and usually cheaper than fresh.
Mixing syrup into hot tea dulls the fruit; wait until the tea is cool.
storage: Keeps 2 days in the fridge; stir before serving. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
